- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot sharp upward spikes in price, then fail to correct downward after the peak.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the 30-day forecast, particularly after mid-forecast period.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model fails to anticipate sharp reversals toward lower levels after peaks.
- Forecast horizon 1–5 days: model is too optimistic; horizon 10–30 days: model is too pessimistic.
- Model often fails to capture the true magnitude of downward corrections after initial spikes.
- Model underestimates the depth of price drops following strong upward moves.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price movements — especially in the 10–20 day window.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to reflect volatility clustering or sudden reversals.
- Model tends to overfit recent high prices, leading to persistent overestimation in early forecast days.
